pairs.subject: agent-instruction-files
pairs.evidence: pipeline/jobfit/repo_scan.py:1099 The scan keeps the target repo's CLAUDE.md out of the harness's instruction channel (claude_cli passes `--setting-sources user` in repo_scan mode), but build_prompt then puts that same foreign file back into the prompt, unfenced and labelled as instructions to a machine reader, so a third-party tree's brief still reaches the agent as steering rather than as data.

techniques.evidence: pipeline/jobfit/repo_scan.py:1099 The technique says that in a tree somebody else owns, the instruction file is data. The prompt calls it 'instructions', and unlike the GitHub review path (fence.ts) and devcase fenced_untrusted it adds no fence and no data-not-instructions clause. No run records or asserts which instruction files were loaded.
pipeline/jobfit/repo_scan.py:891 This module reads other repos' instruction files as scan input. It does not author an always-loaded file of its own, so the admission test has nothing to judge here.

pairs.registryProposal: workspace-ancestry-isolation covers keeping a foreign tree's file out of the loaded set, but it says nothing about a tool that removes the file from discovery and then pastes it into its own prompt. That re-injection path could be stated outright: excerpting a foreign instruction file into a prompt should carry the same 'data, not brief' framing.
